meta.storyTitle: Align historical tests with the retired review contract

summary.prose: Repair historical tests and fixture inventories for the intentionally retired automated-review contract. Assert exact unavailable responses before provider, parser or IO work; preserve generic transport, worker/token, lifecycle, historical-data and temporary-versus-saved persistence coverage through current supported surfaces. Production review execution and RPC classification remain unchanged.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Align historical tests with the retired review contract

errors.condition: Every retired execution, grounding/freshness, lifecycle operation and review step; no provider/IO side effects.

preconditions: Test inputs may be malformed/poisoned to prove no argument inspection.
Do not bypass production refusal through synthetic success mocks on review-named surfaces.
postconditions: Use exact family messages and current error envelopes for daemon, step and MCP boundaries; no start/poll provider review workload.
Move still-valid generic progress/done, synchronous-throw, abort/drain, cwd lookup and worker identity assertions to supported methods or explicitly test-only generic handlers.
Worker token lifecycle covers current analyze/workflow kinds and explicit rejection of retired kinds; preserve session isolation, update/old-token and idle-release assertions for supported kinds.
Current inert historical rendering/metadata and human lifecycle/integrity/build completion gates remain tested, with no fake review entry or provider execution.
Replace deleted fixture paths with real current suites; require child execution evidence and zero live LMDB/Lance artifacts, plus deliberate-opening positive controls.

Persistence repair maps removed writer checks to current guarded sinks and supported entry points: retain hostile-input zero-read/no-write checks at boundaries that guarantee them, and saved artifact/history/cache/trace positives. Do not silently claim a low-level writer offers stronger preflight guarantees than its implementation; any uncovered production defect requires separate triage.

Relationship impact is test-only: tests invoke existing boundaries; daemon owns stores, request owns child/drain lifetime, session owns supported continuation tokens, artifacts retain existing historical records. No production ownership/cardinality/API/IPC/entity/UX change. Prose and assertion mapping suffice; no ERD or companion visual required.

errorCases.detection: Verify path existence, child exit, TAP pass count and no cancellations before checking store absence.
errorCases.response: Replace entry with current real coverage; do not accept empty/failed child runs as isolation proof.
errorCases.userImpact: Trustworthy no-live-store assertions retain deliberate-open positive controls.

errorCases.scenario: Persistence fixture imports removed provenance writer.
errorCases.detection: Module-load failure from original audit; current writer and guarded sink source inspection.
errorCases.response: Remove obsolete import, map valid assertion intent onto current guarded entry/sink and saved persistence control. Keep hostile getters/canaries and reject any claimed safety not actually observed.
errorCases.userImpact: Persistence matrix runs meaningfully rather than failing at import.

errorCases.detection: Reproduce with current supported API and separate from removed contract assumptions.
errorCases.response: Record and route separately; do not relax assertions or change production authority to force this batch green.
errorCases.userImpact: Remaining failures are explicit and linked to correct scope.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test with tsx on supported Node22 under the owned coordinator, serial focused groups. Run baseline before each group's edits; retain actual counts/failures, not blanket skips or longer deadlines. Audit dates back to d7bcd4f9; current checkpoint aa76e132b may expose different later failures. Preserve generic test semantics with an old-assertion→current-control mapping. Typecheck and appropriate source/compiled worker checks; inspect cleanup and final quiescence. No live provider or automatic review session, broad overlapping sweep or release qualification.

migration.stateBefore: Tests mix valid transport/isolation/history assertions with obsolete review execution, labels, tokens, fixture paths and a removed writer import; the historical audit records resulting failures.
migration.stateAfter: Focused tests assert current unavailable responses and preserve surviving semantics through supported operations/current persistence sinks; inventories reference executable suites with genuine isolation controls. Production review behavior and persisted records are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Inventory affected assertions and capture current focused baselines, mapping each legitimate intent to a current supported control before editing.
Migrate backend/client/MCP and worker review-specific assumptions, retaining positive transport/token/lifecycle controls; do not alter RPC classification.

Repair removed writer import and deleted isolation inventories using current boundaries and meaningful saved/temporary/store-opening controls; record any independent production gap rather than weakening tests.
Run serial focused verification, typecheck and needed compiled worker checks; document counts, cleanup, assertion mapping and sibling failures, then obtain human BUILD approval.

migration.backwardCompat: Tests/fixtures only. Current public error text/envelopes, APIs/IPC, token types, artifact formats, model roles and historical data stay unchanged. No data deletion, review restoration, shim exports or production policy bypass.

alternativesConsidered.name: Migrate tests to current contracts
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Separate unavailable-review assertions from supported transport, worker, history and persistence controls.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep review production behavior unchanged. Replace obsolete model-label/execution/token assumptions with exact family-specific rejection and pre-work assertions. Rehome generic transport/lifecycle/worker assertions onto supported analyze/workflow/model operations or test-only handlers. Replace deleted fixture inventory entries with current real suites, and replace removed persistence writer imports with supported guarded storage calls while retaining canary and saved positive controls.
pros: Preserves the intent of meaningful assertions without reviving removed execution.
Uses current contracts and keeps Batch05 RPC classification separate.
cons: Requires explicit mapping of each removed expectation to a surviving control.
Some replacement fixture setup may reveal sibling defects, which must be recorded separately.

alternativesConsidered.name: Compatibility shims for old review fixtures
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Reintroduce old review tokens/writer exports solely to keep historical tests running.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Provide compatibility functions and retained routes that emulate removed review behavior so unchanged tests still receive execution-shaped results.
cons: Violates intentional review retirement and creates production compatibility work solely for obsolete expectations.
Risks restoring provider/IO side effects and misleading test coverage.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Production shims contradict the retired contract.

alternativesConsidered.name: Delete or skip obsolete tests
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Drop any failing test that references review.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Remove review-related suites and their isolation/persistence entries without establishing equivalent current controls.
cons: Loses valid history, cleanup, transport, persistence and store-isolation assertions; violates issue acceptance.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Deletion/skip is not equivalent retained-history or isolation evidence.
